observed: One shared round apparatus disk contains a lower semicylinder with a horizontal flat face, two endpoint mounting rings and one bottom support.
The lower-left source points inward. Its incident arrow reaches the common interface point from below, passing radially through the curved glass boundary.
The reflected arrow leaves the interface point toward the lower right, remains in the glass until its curved-boundary endpoint, and makes the same angle to the normal as the incoming glass segment.
The refracted arrow leaves the same point into upper-right air, further from the normal than the incident ray. It is not drawn as total internal reflection.
The dashed normal crosses the common hit point perpendicular to the flat face.
Air, Glass, Source and Modern schematic are visible English labels. No angle or numerical calibration is fabricated as a readable source label.
The incident, reflected and refracted branches and their three arrowheads remain visible and directionally distinguishable at actual 342px width.
The normal, flat face, curved glass boundary and source housing remain visible; no line-loss artifact is present in this first Chromium screenshot.
All four labels can be read without zoom, clipping or a label/beam collision. Glass is distinguishable beside the lower semicylinder; the diagram is not blank or a black raster.
The 17px base label target agrees with frozen native evidence and the screenshot's screen transform, but this PASS comes from actual first reading, not that number.
